prompt.v: A patient is given 100 mg of a medicine with a half-life of 5 hours. After how many hours are 30 mg left? Give the time to 1 decimal place.

problems.explain: Every 5 hours halves it, so after t hours it is 100 × (1/2) to the power t/5. Set that equal to 30 and divide by 100: (1/2) to the power t/5 is 3/10. Take ln of both sides; the power comes down: (t/5) ln(1/2) = ln(3/10), so t = 5 ln(3/10) / ln(1/2) ≈ 8.6848. So it takes about 8.7 hours.

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 10^(x - 1); options a: log_10(x + 1) | b: log_10(x - 1) | c: log_10(x) + 1 | d: log_10(x) - 1
problems.explain: Write y = 10ˣ⁻¹ and swap x and y: x = 10 to the power y − 1. The log undoes the power first, y − 1 = log x, and then y = log x + 1. (The −1 is inside the power, so it is undone after the log, outside it: log(x + 1) puts it back inside.) So f⁻¹(x) = log x + 1.

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 10^(x - 1); options a: log_10(x - 1) | b: log_10(x) - 1 | c: log_10(x) + 1 | d: log_10(x + 1)
problems.explain: Write y = 10ˣ⁻¹ and swap x and y: x = 10 to the power y − 1. The log undoes the power first, y − 1 = log x, and then y = log x + 1. (The −1 is inside the power, so it is undone after the log, outside it: log(x + 1) puts it back inside.) So f⁻¹(x) = log x + 1.

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 10^x + 4; options a: log_10(x) + 4 | b: log_10(x - 4) | c: log_10(x) - 4 | d: log_10(x + 4)
problems.explain: Write y = 10ˣ + 4 and swap x and y: x = 10ʸ + 4. Take 4 away first, 10ʸ = x − 4, then the power, as a log: y = log(x − 4). (log x − 4 undoes the steps in the wrong order.) So f⁻¹(x) = log(x − 4).

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 10^x - 3; options a: log_10(x) - 3 | b: log_10(x + 3) | c: log_10(x) + 3 | d: log_10(x - 3)
problems.explain: Write y = 10ˣ − 3 and swap x and y: x = 10ʸ − 3. Add 3 first, 10ʸ = x + 3, then the power, as a log: y = log(x + 3). (log x + 3 undoes the steps in the wrong order.) So f⁻¹(x) = log(x + 3).

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 10^x/4; options a: log_10(x/4) | b: 4*log_10(x) | c: log_10(x)/4 | d: log_10(4x)
problems.explain: Write y = 10ˣ/4 and swap x and y: x = 10ʸ/4. Undo the ÷4 first, 10ʸ = 4x, then the power: y = log(4x). (4 log x undoes the steps in the wrong order.) So f⁻¹(x) = log(4x).

problems.text: log inverse: f(x) = 3^(4x); options a: log_3(x)/4 | b: log_3(4x) | c: 4*log_3(x) | d: log_3(x/4)
problems.explain: Write y = 3⁴ˣ and swap x and y: x = 3 to the power 4y. The log undoes the power first, 4y = log₃ x, then divide by 4: y = (log₃ x)/4. (log₃(x/4) undoes the steps in the wrong order.) So f⁻¹(x) = (log₃ x)/4.

problems.explain: The graph runs down beside the line x = −1, where the inside of the log is 0: so the inside is x + 1, not x − 1. It passes through (0, 1), where the inside is 1 and the log is 0, so 1 is what is added outside; and through (1, 2), where the inside is 2 and the log is 1. So the graph is y = log₂(x + 1) + 1.
